From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contingency runbook & commitment reset — MAP update

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. We heard the concerns about the lab evaluation schedule slipping and how that compresses your go-live window. Per our commitment, I pulled together a short contingency runbook and proposed a commitment reset for the MAP so you have a clear path to close without exposing the pilot to quality risk.

Attached: commitment_grid_v2.xlsx (matrix of milestones + owners) and a one-page MAP revision. High level:
- Option A (preferred): 1-week shift to the customer-eval window, Redwood provides prioritised inference capacity during the extended validation window and a single rollback snapshot.
- Option B: Keep original date, but Redwood delivers after-hours support + 2 additional eval tokens per session to accelerate turnover.

As next steps: please confirm which option you prefer by EOD Friday (7/31). If neither works, we should escalate to a short executive alignment call to re-baseline commercial commitments.

Quick ask for you, Erin: can procurement confirm typical DocuSign lead times on your side? I included procurement on the thread for transparency.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the clear options. After talking with the evaluation team, we lean toward Option A (the one-week shift). The main constraint is our internal compliance window — we need that extra time to complete the audit checklist.

Procurement: our signing SLA is typically 3–5 business days once a final DocuSign arrives. I flagged the opportunity as high priority.

Can you confirm Redwood’s committed turnaround time for applying the priority capacity and what the rollback snapshot cadence looks like?

—Erin

Team — forwarding Nimbus response. They picked Option A and procurement expects 3–5 business days for DocuSign.

Quick internal notes / risk table I'm proposing to publish to the customer as a short live document (I'll attach updated MAP):
- Risk 1: Evaluation compliance checklist incomplete — impact: 7-day slip; mitigation: Redwood provides prioritized infra and a single rollback snapshot.
- Risk 2: Procurement delay — impact: 3–10 day slip; mitigation: provide pre-signed SOW stub and escalate to contracts SME for parallel review.
- Risk 3: Integration bug found in smoke tests — impact: variable; mitigation: limited debug window + rotating on-call during customer eval weeks.

Recommendation: 1-week re-baseline (new target close 2026-08-14) with a hard escalation point 48 hours before cutover to loop in Avery for executive decisioning. I attached the updated MAP I intend to send after internal alignment (MAP_revision_2026-08-10.pdf).

Marissa — can you confirm CS capacity for the extended window? Karthik — please confirm we can reserve the dedicated capacity in the preferred region and note any cost delta. Laura — please review the recommended escalation language (I want to be conservative here).

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: MAP_revision_2026-08-10.pdf

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed the proposed runbook and the risk table. I approve the 1-week re-baseline to 2026-08-14 under these conditions:
- Redwood provides the prioritized capacity at no additional charge for the first two business days of the extended window (to reduce evaluation friction).
- If procurement exceeds 7 business days to sign, we revert to Option B but keep the extended support terms for the same period.
- Contracts will prepare a DocuSign envelope and a pre-signed SOW stub; Ben, loop in Contracts immediately.

Ben — please send the updated MAP and the DocuSign link to Erin and procurement. Marissa — confirm CS on-call schedule for 8/10–8/18. Karthik — confirm capacity reservation and any required budget code so Finance can reconcile.

I'll join a 15-minute alignment call if procurement signals a delay beyond 3 business days.
